demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Triggers.value: A specific texture associated with the event

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Watching TV programmes/ films or reading about similar events
I dwell on how the event could have been prevented
perform mental rituals to prevent bad things from happening again

Threat.value: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
Being superalert or watchful or on guard
I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong

Negative Appraisals.value: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
I have failed in my most important role in life
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: For trauma involving the unexpected death of a loved one, the trigger 'being forced to do something' is hard to link to the trauma narrative given the rest of the profile. The other triggers (sleeping alone, specific texture) fit grief/PTSD better, but loss of autonomy suggests a different trauma theme such as coercion or assault and is not supported elsewhere in the selected items.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: The threat items are dominated by abrupt physical-startle cues (movement nearby, unexpected touch), which more strongly suggest interpersonal violence or attack-related danger. In a bereavement-related PTSD profile, these can occur, but here they are not grounded by matching triggers, appraisals, or memory content, making the threat pattern clinically incoherent with the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
issues.explanation: 'I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible' is poorly integrated with the rest of the profile. The negative appraisals otherwise center on loss of meaning and failure in a valued role after bereavement, whereas fear of violent loss of control introduces a different clinical theme that is not supported by the trigger, threat, memory, or coping items.

issues.item: Sleeping Alone: Sleeping alone or in an unfamiliar place
issues.explanation: 'Sleeping alone or in an unfamiliar place' is not a coherent trigger for the stated trauma of traumatic bereavement in the context of the rest of the profile. The other triggers are grief- and event-linked (funerals/graves, specific texture), whereas sleeping alone implies a threat/safety formulation more typical of assault, combat, or home invasion trauma. With this trauma type and the selected threat items, a clinician would question why this is a central trigger.

issues.item: Fear of Rage: I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible
issues.explanation: 'I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible' sits poorly with the rest of the profile. The profile is dominated by grief, guilt/failed-role appraisals, hypervigilant false-alarm threat responses, and prevention-focused rumination/rituals. A fear of committing serious rage-driven harm introduces a qualitatively different concern that is not supported by the triggers, memory content, or strategies selected, making the appraisal set internally less coherent.
